trigger: Gate 1 Resource Ledger for the C++ files in this range
summary: RESOURCE LEDGER — NO owning raw-resource boundary is added, transferred or released by this range. Acquisitions: none. New state: one std::function member (classify_fn_) on DashboardRoutes, borrowed non-owning pointers (mgmt_group_store_, metrics_) that outlive the route sink, and stack-local std::optional/std::vector/std::string. No fd, HANDLE, SOCKET, FILE*, SQLite stmt, OpenSSL/BCrypt object, C-string, thread, subprocess or temp path is created or destroyed. No manual cleanup, so the non-RAII floor does not apply. No callback-lifetime change: classify_fn_ is assigned before register_routes in production and captured by a handler that captures ServerImpl*, which strictly outlives the sink — same shape as the pre-existing fleet_read_fn_/resolve_fn_ members. CommandCapability holds string_views into constexpr catalogue arrays with static storage, and the dashboard never reads gate.capability, so no borrowed-data escape either way. confine_destructive_targets takes its argument by const& and the returned vector is fully constructed before the move-assign to agent_ids.

trigger: a dashboard automation owner follows upgrading.md's remediation
summary: upgrading.md told dashboard callers to send explicit agent_ids; POST /api/dashboard/execute has no such field and ignores one. A single agent is scope=<agent-id>. Following the guide left the dispatch refused. Codex derived HIGH via I4; adjudicated to MEDIUM/SHOULD on Kimi's reasoning that the wrong remediation FAILS SAFE (dispatch stays refused, no damage) so I6 is the honest impact, not I4. Fixed by splitting the remediation and the Verify step by surface.

trigger: incident responder follows audit-log.md to reconstruct a refused dispatch's blast radius
summary: The audit row's caveat claimed the requested agent_ids/scope reach the server log; the scope_violation arm audited but never logged, so the requested target was in NEITHER channel. Adjudicated MEDIUM/SHOULD (evidence-location misdirection, not guidance into a harmful act). Fixed on the CODE side rather than by weakening the doc: the confinement arm now logs the sanitised, capped requested agent ids, so the documented contract is true and incident response gains the blast radius it could not previously reconstruct.

trigger: reading audit-log.md's sanitisation claim against the dashboard emitter
summary: audit-log.md claimed both caller-supplied fields are sanitised and capped at 128 bytes — true of the REST twin, false of the dashboard's three new denial arms, which wrote plugin/action raw. Reachable arms carry catalogue-bounded values so no injection is demonstrable. Fixed on the CODE side to match the documented contract: all three dashboard audit details now route plugin and action through onbehalf::sanitize_for_log(...,128), matching server.cpp's REST arm.

trigger: a regression in the dashboard Targeted arm is tested on a no-PG macOS/Windows leg
summary: The only route-level test proving a Destructive action DOES still dispatch to a legitimately-targeted agent is Postgres-gated, so it skips on macOS and Windows; a route mutation making the Targeted arm always refuse would leave every local run green. NOT FIXED, deliberately. ManagementGroupStore requires a pg::PgPool& and get_visible_agents is non-virtual, so no test-only path exists — closing this would mean adding a new injectable seam into the CONFINEMENT path. That path is catastrophic-if-violated per the #1788 routed-concern row, and a seam added after the adversarial gate had already run would ship unreviewed by it, to close a finding both reviewers graded LOW. Accepted instead: the PG-enabled Linux CI leg asserts the exact send set {"dev-A"}, the pure helper confine_destructive_targets is directly tested, and the #1788 exact-send-set binding lives in test_dispatch_confined_arms.cpp. Follow-up issue to be filed when remote work resumes: add an always-running route fixture on the test_dispatch_confined_arms.cpp:567-590 no-database precedent, designed and reviewed as its own change.
